topic.subject: social
topic.title: The Earth in the solar system
topic.scope: planets, Earth as a unique planet, Moon, asteroids, meteoroids, satellites

misconceptions.statement: Stars are small, twinkling objects that are stuck to the sky.
misconceptions.why: They appear tiny due to immense distance and seem fixed against the night sky backdrop.
misconceptions.fix: Stars are massive, burning balls of gas like our Sun, located extremely far away from Earth.

probe.question: If we traveled in a rocket towards a star, would it get bigger?
probe.wrong_answer: No, stars are just tiny lights in the sky.

misconceptions.statement: All planets in the solar system have life like Earth.
misconceptions.why: Students often project human-centric experiences onto other celestial bodies in science fiction.
misconceptions.fix: Earth is the only known planet in our solar system with the right temperature, water, and air to support life.

probe.question: Could humans survive on Jupiter?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, it is a planet like Earth, so it must have people.

misconceptions.statement: The Sun revolves around the Earth.
misconceptions.why: Our daily observation shows the Sun rising and setting, making it look like the Sun is moving.
misconceptions.fix: The Earth rotates on its axis and revolves around the Sun, which is the center of the solar system.

probe.question: Why does the Sun move across the sky during the day?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the Sun travels around the Earth every day.

misconceptions.statement: The Moon produces its own light like a star.
misconceptions.why: The Moon appears bright in the night sky, and children associate brightness with self-illumination.
misconceptions.fix: The Moon does not have its own light; it reflects the light of the Sun.

probe.question: Where does the Moon get its light from?
probe.wrong_answer: It makes its own light because it glows at night.

misconceptions.statement: The Moon changes its shape throughout the month.
misconceptions.why: Visual observation of phases makes it appear as if the physical shape of the Moon is changing.
misconceptions.fix: The Moon's physical shape stays the same; we only see different parts of its sunlit half as it orbits Earth.

probe.question: Why does the Moon look like a crescent sometimes?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the Moon actually shrinks and grows during the month.
